IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

 PRESENT:

 THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE K.HARILAL
 &
 THE HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE A.M.BABU

 MONDAY, THE 18TH DAY OF JUNE 2018 / 28TH JYAISHTA, 1940

 MAT.APPEAL.NO. 155 OF 2007
 -------------------
 AGAINST THE ORDER/JUDGMENT IN OP 387/2003 OF FAMILY COURT, KANNUR DATED
 06-10-2006
 ----------------------


APPELLANT(S)/APPELLANT/PETITIONER


 JOSEKURIYAN PULLIALIEKAL
 CHUNDA P.O., VAYAKKARA, PULINGOM DESOM,, TALIPARAMBA.


 BY ADV.SRI.V.N.RAMESAN NAMBISAN



RESPONDENT(S)/RESPONDENT:


 SOFI JOSE KAITHOTTUNGAL,
 D/O, VARGHESE,
 KAITHOTTUNGAL, ALAKODE, VAYATTUPARAMBA P.O.,,
 TALIPARAMBA TALUK.

 BY ADVS. SRI.K.R.AVINASH (KUNNATH)
 SRI.ABDUL RAOOF PALLIPATH


 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 18-06-2018,
THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:




DXY

 K.HARILAL & A.M.BABU, JJ.
 ----------------------------------------
 Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007
 ------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 18th day of June, 2018



 JUDGMENT

Harilal, J


 Appellant is the husband of the respondent. He filed

O.P.387/2003 before the family court, Kannur, seeking a decree

for dissolution of marriage under Sec.10(iii) and (x) of the Divorce

Act, 1869 . The respondent resisted the said application and both

parties adduced evidence to prove their rival contentions. After

considering the evidence on record, the family court dismissed the

petition on a finding that the appellant miserably failed to prove

that the respondent has been incurably of unsound mind for a

continuous period not less than two years immediately preceding

the presentation of the petition. This appeal has been filed

challenging the said findings whereby the family court dismissed

the original petition.

2. Brief facts of the case can be summarized as follows :
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

According to the appellant, his marriage with the

respondent was solemnized on 17.2.1992 as per the customary

rites and practices prevailing in Christian community and two

children are born out of the said wedlock. Immediately a few

days after the marriage, the appellant came to note that the

respondent is a person with abnormal character and behaviour.

She did not have normal attitude and feeling of a newly wedded

woman. She was very rude and rustic from the very beginning

and from the next day of the marriage itself she picked up

quarrels with the appellant and his family members. She never

had any love and affection towards the appellant or his family

members. The appellant found difficulty to adjust with the

behaviour of the respondent but he tolerated her cruel behaviour

to maintain the marital life. When she came to know that she is

suffering from some kind of mental ailments, she was taken to

mental hospitals. When the mental condition of the respondent

became worse, on 22.1.1992 he took the respondent to medical

college hospital, Pariyaram and she was admitted there and
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::3::

treated as an inpatient. Thereafter, she was taken to Kasthurba

hospital, Manipal where she was admitted on 23.2.1998 and got

discharged on 28.2.1998. After about six months, she was again

taken to Sacred Heart hospital, Painkulam where she was

admitted on 30.11.1998 and treated as an inpatient for 20 days.

After discharging from the hospital, she was treated as an

inpatient also. When the illness got aggravated at times, she was

put under medical care at local hospitals. Again, on 20.8.2002

she was again taken to Sacred Heart hospital, Painkulam and

treated there as an inpatient for 20 days. There, the doctor

opined that her illness cannot be cured permanently. From the

hospital, she was taken to her house and put under medication.

Ever since the petitioner and the children are residing

separately. Thereafter, the mental illness of the respondent again

got aggravated and she was again taken to mental hospital,

Calicut where she was admitted as an inpatient for some time

and she was under treatment even at the time of filing the

petition. Ever since the marriage, the petitioner was suffering
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::4::

utmost cruelty, both physical and mental, at the hands of the

respondent till her departure from his company in the year 2002.

She caused maximum mental stress and strain to him while they

were cohabited together. She used abusive language against the

petitioner in front of his relatives and children. She alleged

immorality against him even in front of his children and

relatives. The children are studying in school. The petitioner

cannot suffer any more cruelty at the hands of the respondent

and he has lost all his controls in having a married life with the

respondent who is suffering from mental disease. In the above

context, the petitioner was constrained to file the original

petition seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground that the

respondent has been incurably of unsound mind for a

continuous period of not less than two years.

3. The respondent filed counter-statement, denying the

mental illness alleged against her by the appellant. According to

her, the statement that from the very beginning of the marriage,

her behaviour was abnormal is incorrect and she was not rude or
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::5::

rustic, as alleged by the appellant. She was not violent towards

the appellant, as alleged by him. The appellant and the

respondent had a normal family life, though the appellant

treated her with cruelty on a false allegation that she was

suffering from some kind of mental problem. The appellant and

his family were bent upon to destroy the mental framework of

the respondent and to make her a lunatic. In the meanwhile, the

respondent gave birth to two children and she looked after the

children, as that of any other mother. After the marriage, the

appellant demanded more money and gold ornaments. But, her

father was not prepared to honour this unreasonable demand.

So, the respondent had to suffer cruelty at the hands of the

appellant. She admitted that she was treated as an inpatient in

hospital referred to in the Original Petition. But, actually she

had no such mental illness. She was taken to different hospitals

at the instance of the appellant. The appellant and his relatives

unreasonably misbranded her as a mentally unsound wife,

without any basis. According to her, she never behaved rashly or
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::6::

cruelly towards the appellant in front of the children or relatives

and friends. She has not picked up quarrel always as alleged by

the appellant. The appellant had never shown any love or

affection towards the respondent. The allegation that the

respondent had mental ailment even before the marriage is false.

She was not suspicious of the appellant, as alleged by him. She

never accused the appellant any immoral relations with any

other woman. The allegation that the respondent had psychiatric

complaint and she was mentally ill and treated in different

hospitals before the marriage is not correct. She is fit both

physically and mentally. Thus, the respondent denied all the

allegations levelled against her as grounds for getting the

marriage dissolved.

4. Both parties adduced evidence. The appellant was

examined as AW.1 and two other witnesses were examined as

AW.2 and AW.3. AW.2 is an independent witness and AW.3 is

the Doctor, who treated the respondent for the alleged mental

illness. Exts.A1 to A4(c) and X1 to X2 were marked from the part
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::7::

of the appellant and the respondent was examined as RW.1. On

an appraisal of the aforesaid evidence, the Family Court found

that the appellant/petitioner failed to prove that the respondent

has been incurably of unsound mind for a continuous period not

less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of

the petition. The findings whereby the Family Court rejected the

prayer for dissolution of marriage, are assailed in this appeal.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the

learned counsel for the respondent.

6. On an analysis of the impugned judgment under

challenge, it could be seen that the Family Court has rejected the

prayer for dissolution of marriage on a finding that the appellant

failed to plead and prove the facts constituting statutory

requirements, to get the marriage dissolved under Section 10(iii) 

of the Act. The statutory requirement to get the marriage

dissolved under Section 10(iii) of the Act is that the respondent

has been incurably of unsound mind for a continuous period not

less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::8::

the petition. Therefore, the point to be considered in the instant

case is, can the Family Court be justified in rejecting the prayer

for dissolution of marriage on the ground that the appellant has

failed to plead and prove the facts constituting statutory

requirements as contemplated under Section 10(iii) of the Act?

We have meticulously gone through the averments in the

Original Petition. According to the averments in the petition, the

appellant admitted that they have lived together as husband and

wife from 1992-2002 and two children were born out of the said

wedlock. From the very beginning of the marriage, he came to

know that the respondent is a person with abnormal character

and behaviour and subsequently, the said abnormal behaviour

became aggravated and she was taken to different hospitals

during different periods for the treatment of her mental illness.

7. As rightly pointed out by the Family Court, it is

relevant to note that nowhere in the petition, the appellant made

out a case that the respondent was of unsound mind. On an

analysis of the statutory provisions, we find that the incurable
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::9::

condition of the unsound mind and the continuity of such a mind

for a period not less than two years immediately preceding the

presentation of the petition are relevant factors constituting the

statutory requirements to get the marriage dissolved. Nothing

has been averred in the Original Petition so as to constitute

aforesaid relevant factors, envisaged under Section 10(iii) of the

Act.

8. Coming to the instant case, the Original Petition was

filed on 06.10.2006. In the Original Petition itself the appellant

admitted that they lived together up to 28.03.2002. Thus,

admittedly the Original Petition was filed four years after the

departure of the respondent from the company of the appellant.

It is true that the appellant has specifically averred the

treatment, which was given to the respondent from 22.01.1998 to

31.05.2004. There is no pleadings as regards any kind of

treatment for which the respondent had undergone after

31.05.2004. All the averments disclosing specific incidents of

abnormal behaviour or mental illness relates to the period up to
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::10::

April,2002, as she was not residing with the appellant after

2002. The point to be considered is, whether the appellant has

succeeded to prove that the respondent was incurably of

unsound mind for a period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006 i.e,

two years immediately preceding the presentation of the

petition?

9. It has come out in pleadings and evidence in Exts.X1

and X2 that when her behaviour got aggravated at first, she was

taken to hospital on 28.02.2002. Ext.X1 as well as Ext.X2 and

Ext.A1 series of documents would prove that the respondent had

some kind of mental ailment from 1998 and she was treated up

to 31.05.2004. Ext.X1 is the photostat copy of the case records of

the respondent from S.H. Hospital, Paynkulam. As per Ext.X1,

the treatment starts from 30.11.1998 and ends on 31.07.2002.

10. None of the entries would show any kind of treatment

during the period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006. Similarly,

Ext.X2 shows the particulars of the treatment which was given to

the respondent in Government Mental Health Center,
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::11::

Kozhikkode. As per the entries, the treatment starts 30.05.2003,

as it is the date of admission. The last entry is dated on

26.05.2004. Neither Ext.X1 nor Ext.X2, discloses any entry to

the effect that the respondent has been incurably of unsound

mind and she was treated for that. Thus on analysis on Exts.X1

and X2, it is discernible that the respondent was not treated for

any kind of unsound mind, during the period from 06.10.2004

to 06.10.2006. Thus, there is no pleadings or evidence to prove

that the respondent was suffering from incurable unsound mind

for a period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

11. Coming to oral evidence, the petitioner has given

evidence as PW1 and he has sworn a chief affidavit in terms with

the averments in the original petition. But, the averments in the

original petition disclosing the abnormal behavior of the

petitioner are confined to a period from 1992 to 2002 only as

they lived together upto 28.02.2002 only. Therefore, even if the

oral evidence given by the appellant is taken at its face value. It

can be his experience with the respondent while he was residing
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::12::

together upto 2002 only. In other words, absolutely there is no

oral evidence relating to the mental condition of the respondent

during the period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

12. AW2 is an independent witness and she was examined

to prove the alleged violent and abnormal behavior of the

respondent. It has come out in evidence that the respondent has

been residing separately from 2002 onwards. AW2 is a lady

who is residing near the house of the petitioner from 2002

onwards only. It is true that in chief examination she deposed

that she had several occasion to witness the violent behaviour of

the respondent and she herself was a victim of physical assault

by the respondent. She deposed that the respondent had

resided near to the house of the AW2 for 3 years from 2002.

But, the appellant has no case that they were resided together

after 28.03.2002. Thus, we find that AW2 had deposed against

the admitted case of the petitioner that they have been residing

separately from April 2002 onwards. If they were living

separately from April 2002 onwards, AW2 who started to live
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::13::

near the house of the petitioner from 2002 had no occasion to

witness the alleged abnormal behaviour of the respondent. That

apart, the evidence of AW2 cannot be relied on in view of the

evidence of RW1. RW1 in her evidence, specifically stated that

once she assaulted AW2 when she interfered with the family

matters of the respondent. It gives rise to inference that the

AW2 was nursing hostility against the respondent and she is not

an independent witness. We are of the opinion that the evidence

of AW2 can never be believed as it is untrustworthy.

13. As far as unsound mind of a person, the medical

evidence is crucial. AW3 is the doctor who treated the

respondent. In chief examination AW3 has stated that the

respondent was treated as an inpatient in his hospital on

13.11.1998 for 20 days but according to him, on medication the

mental illness can be cured. The last date of the treatment was

on 19.11.2002 and on that day he had written in Ext.X1 that the

respondent was having no problems and after that he didn't see

her. Thus the doctor is unaware of the mental condition of the
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::14::

respondent during the period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

As regards the nature and gravity of the mental illness of the

respondent, AW2 unambiguously stated that the respondents

illness is curable by medication. Thus, absolutely there is no oral

evidence disclosing the mental condition of the respondent for a

period of 2 years from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

14. Though, it has come out in evidence that the

respondent was treated for some kind of mental illness, the

entries in Exts.X1 and X2, do not show that the respondent has

been incurably of unsound mind during that period. The doctor

who adduced the medical evidence also deposed that the mental

illness of the respondent is curable by medication.

15. As we have held above, the incurable nature of the

unsound mind and the continuity of 2 years with such an

unsound mind, immediately proceeding the presentation of the

petition are indispensable to get a decree for dissolution of

marriage under Section 10 (1) (iii) of the Divorce Act 1869. In

the instant case it has come out in evidence that the respondent
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::15::

was treated for some kind of mental illness for a period from

1998 to April 2004 and that mental illness was a curable one by

medication.

16. Absolutely, there is no evidence to prove that the

respondent has been of unsound mind for a period of 2 years

starting from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006. In the above analysis

the family court is justified in finding that the appellant failed to

prove that the respondent has been incurably of unsound mind

for a continues period of not less than 2 years, immediately

proceedings presentation of the petition. We do not find any

reason to interfere with the same.
Hence, this Mat. Appeal is dismissed.
Sd/-

K.HARILAL, JUDGE

 Sd/-

A.M.BABU, JUDGE
Mrcs/DST/Dxy

to prove the alleged violent and abnormal behavior of the

respondent. It has come out in evidence that the respondent has

been residing separately from 2002 onwards. AW2 is a lady

who is residing near the house of the petitioner from 2002

onwards only. It is true that in chief examination she deposed

that she had several occasion to witness the violent behaviour of

the respondent and she herself was a victim of physical assault

by the respondent. She deposed that the respondent had

resided near to the house of the AW2 for 3 years from 2002.

[p_14] But, the appellant has no case that they were resided together

after 28.03.2002. Thus, we find that AW2 had deposed against

the admitted case of the petitioner that they have been residing

separately from April 2002 onwards. If they were living

separately from April 2002 onwards, AW2 who started to live
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::13::

[blockquote_21] near the house of the petitioner from 2002 had no occasion to

witness the alleged abnormal behaviour of the respondent. That

apart, the evidence of AW2 cannot be relied on in view of the

evidence of RW1. RW1 in her evidence, specifically stated that

once she assaulted AW2 when she interfered with the family

matters of the respondent. It gives rise to inference that the

AW2 was nursing hostility against the respondent and she is not

an independent witness. We are of the opinion that the evidence

of AW2 can never be believed as it is untrustworthy.

[blockquote_22] 13. As far as unsound mind of a person, the medical

evidence is crucial. AW3 is the doctor who treated the

respondent. In chief examination AW3 has stated that the

respondent was treated as an inpatient in his hospital on

13.11.1998 for 20 days but according to him, on medication the

mental illness can be cured. The last date of the treatment was

on 19.11.2002 and on that day he had written in Ext.X1 that the

respondent was having no problems and after that he didn't see

her. Thus the doctor is unaware of the mental condition of the
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::14::

[blockquote_24] respondent during the period from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

As regards the nature and gravity of the mental illness of the

respondent, AW2 unambiguously stated that the respondents

illness is curable by medication. Thus, absolutely there is no oral

evidence disclosing the mental condition of the respondent for a

period of 2 years from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006.

[blockquote_25] 14. Though, it has come out in evidence that the

respondent was treated for some kind of mental illness, the

entries in Exts.X1 and X2, do not show that the respondent has

been incurably of unsound mind during that period. The doctor

who adduced the medical evidence also deposed that the mental

illness of the respondent is curable by medication.

[blockquote_26] 15. As we have held above, the incurable nature of the

unsound mind and the continuity of 2 years with such an

unsound mind, immediately proceeding the presentation of the

petition are indispensable to get a decree for dissolution of

marriage under Section 10 (1) (iii) of the Divorce Act 1869. In

the instant case it has come out in evidence that the respondent
Mat.Appeal.No. 155 of 2007

 ::15::

[blockquote_28] was treated for some kind of mental illness for a period from

1998 to April 2004 and that mental illness was a curable one by

medication.

[blockquote_29] 16. Absolutely, there is no evidence to prove that the

respondent has been of unsound mind for a period of 2 years

starting from 06.10.2004 to 06.10.2006. In the above analysis

the family court is justified in finding that the appellant failed to

prove that the respondent has been incurably of unsound mind

for a continues period of not less than 2 years, immediately

proceedings presentation of the petition. We do not find any

reason to interfere with the same.

[p_16] Hence, this Mat. Appeal is dismissed.
